alignments.note: Connective δέ realized by the verse-opening And.
Quantifier πᾶς takes every; the ASV writes a second English word (man) for the article, so rule 80's single-word compression does not apply and the ordinary split of rules 22 and 32 holds.
Substantival article before a participle supplies the nominal word and nothing else (rules 22, 32, 80): man is the article's, the relativizer belongs to the participle.

Participle rendered as a finite relative clause: that is a rule 7/31 helper on the participle. The supplied in the games completes the athletic sense of ἀγωνίζομαι itself and no other token licenses it (rules 7, 103), so it rides inside this unit; head on the verb word striveth per rule 17. Marking in the games added remains defensible, but no source token is spent that would license it elsewhere.
Support-verb rendering: exerciseth carries no sense of its own and self control is the meaning-bearing complement, so rule 17 heads on control (as bear witness heads on witness).

Accusative of respect; the supplied in realizes the case and stays with the anarthrous word under rule 21's determinerless clause. Rule 17's generic-noun clause heads a substantival adjective expanded with things on all.

Correlative μέν: the ASV writes no indeed, and marking the correlation elsewhere is not writing it (rule 70). A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement; that report is not a correction.

The Greek clause has no finite main verb; the ASV supplies do it. The expressed subject is a substantival demonstrative, which falls on rule 53's pronoun side under rule 68 and carries the supplied verb itself (cf. τοῦτο … τρίτον → This is now the third time). Folding do it onto λάβωσιν remains defensible, but that verb already has its own English word receive.
Purpose ἵνα realized by the infinitival to that introduces its English clause (rule 40); the verb stands alone.
Subjunctive rendered by the bare infinitive receive, its marker having gone to ἵνα under rule 40.
Attributive adjective takes a bare corruptible; the supplied determiner belongs to the noun under rule 58.
Anarthrous noun takes the supplied indefinite determiner under rules 51 and 58, headed on the noun.
Emphatic nominative pronoun takes we; the clause's verb is elliptical in Greek and the ASV supplies none.
The noun is elliptical, so the adjective is substantival in the English and takes the supplied determiner as an ordinary rule 51 helper on the anarthrous word it determines.

review_notes: s008 μέν is the only unrepresented unit; every other source token and all 27 target tokens are partitioned exactly once.
πᾶς ὁ ἀγωνιζόμενος is split three ways under rules 22, 32 and 80 because the ASV wrote a separate English word for the article (man) rather than compressing the pair into whosoever.

Two judgment calls are recorded in the unit notes: in the games folded onto ἀγωνιζόμενος rather than marked added, and the supplied do it placed on the demonstrative subject under rule 68 rather than on λάβωσιν.
